constants.gauge_note: a point gauge throughout: sawtooth.py showed 5 and 10 mm gauges change the spread by under 1 pp, so the strip is the only length being varied here

headline.hypothesis: an integral over a whole number of crack spacings should average the sawtooth out, so the 100 mm strip is simply too narrow
headline.verdict: refused: widening the strip removes most of the phase SPREAD and leaves the phase MEAN wrong by 20 to 37 pp, because the sawtooth is passed through the pointwise constitutive map element by element before any strip integral is taken, and a nonlinear map does not commute with an average
headline.confound_verdict: widening is nearly free on a smooth field inside the D-region, so the confound is not what stops it
headline.one_spacing_caveat: a gauge of exactly one spacing returns the stored strain by construction, as sawtooth.py records; what is measured here and is not by construction is the tolerance around it, and the fact that the strip cannot substitute for it
headline.practitioner: the requirement is on the length the fibre is averaged over before it enters the model, not on the length of the instrumented cut: a running mean over one crack spacing, held to about 10 per cent, with the strip a weak second-order help once the gauge is right
